clue.text: Odd about Penny, American, visiting Morecambe perhaps

indicators.note: the pieces before it are guests staying inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, so his first name is Eric
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a cent is the American penny coin

explanation.surface: Someone strange, with a penny from the States, drops in on a seaside town or comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire seaside town, but here it stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe; 'visiting' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something odd is unconventional and peculiar, which is the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Horse discovered adorned with spangles

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, the outer letters taken off

parts.note: sequined describes clothing decorated with sequins, small spangles

explanation.surface: A horse uncovered, adorned with glittering spangles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the cover, the S and D, off SEQUINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means of horses, and as a noun is a member of the horse family.

clue.text: Admiral's first aboard damaged escort vessel

indicators.note: aboard means on a ship, so the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
damaged means broken, so the letters of escort are rearranged
first takes only the initial letter of admiral

explanation.surface: An admiral is first aboard a damaged escort ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges ESCORT into COSTER; 'aboard' puts the A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaster is a ship carrying cargo along the coast, so a type of vessel.

clue.text: Country dinner rather long mostly to prepare

indicators.note: to prepare means to make ready, so the letters are reworked
mostly means all but the last letter of long

explanation.surface: A dinner taking rather long to prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LONG to LON; 'to prepare' rearranges DINNER, RATHER and LON.
explanation.definitionFit: Northern Ireland is one of the four countries of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Uncensored idiotic claims repeated

indicators.note: claims means takes hold of, so the run of letters is held within the words

explanation.surface: An uncensored, idiotic set of claims repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated means did again, the past tense of redo.

clue.text: Narrow escape from heavy hail

parts.note: close weather is heavy, humid and oppressive
to hail is to call out to someone

explanation.surface: A narrow escape from a heavy hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy' and 'hail' look like weather; they are CLOSE (muggy) and CALL (shout to).
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is an idiom for a narrow escape from danger.

clue.text: Coffee mug daughter upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A girl knocks over a mug of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FACED round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decaf is a caffeine-free coffee, short for decaffeinated.

clue.text: Wife seems ideal to disperse fungal problem

parts.note: my old Dutch is Cockney slang for wife

indicators.note: to disperse means to scatter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife seems ideal at dispersing a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' for wife is old Cockney slang (Duchess of Fife); 'to disperse' rearranges SEEMS IDEAL into ELM DISEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch elm disease is a fungal infection that killed most of Britain's elm trees.

clue.text: Game bird that in Spain one hears

indicators.note: one hears means the words are said aloud

parts.note: a crow is a bird; que is Spanish for that

explanation.surface: A game bird that one hears in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one phrase, but Game is the definition. Said aloud, CROW plus QUE (kay) gives the garden game.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is a lawn game of hitting balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Keen to promote English food? It's extremely difficult

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, so the English letter moves earlier

parts.note: a fine or keen edge is a sharp one
a dish is food served

explanation.surface: An eager campaign to promote English food proves very hard.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE DISH has its E 'promoted' a place forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilishly hard, as with a tough puzzle.

clue.text: Song penned by a French journalist, not previously broadcast

parts.note: un is French for a
an air is a song or tune
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A French reporter writes a song that has never been aired.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme not yet transmitted on radio or TV has never been put on air.

clue.text: Issue of Oxford University book retaining copyright

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the book holds the copyright symbol inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book
C is the copyright symbol, a C in a circle

explanation.surface: A university press publishing a book under copyright.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue can mean a result or consequence, the end product of events.

clue.text: Nick naturally has love for area

indicators.note: love is put in place of area, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: natch is informal shorthand for naturally
love means zero in tennis scores, so O

explanation.surface: A man named Nick naturally has a passion for his region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has love for area' says replace the A of NATCH with an O.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove, and so is a notch.

clue.text: Greek character behind banker and German dog

indicators.note: the Greek letter comes behind, after, the river

parts.note: a banker is crossword slang for a river, something with banks; the Dee is a British river
rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
und is German for and

explanation.surface: A Greek man who follows a banker and a German around like a hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier but a river, the Dee, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A deerhound is a large rough-coated Scottish hunting breed.

clue.text: Painters like Millais perhaps worked outside best, artist admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the artist goes inside the rest
the rearranged letters sit outside, around, the word for best
worked means shaped or fashioned, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Victorian painters perhaps produced their best work with an artist joining them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' signals the anagram of the fodder, which 'outside' wraps round the word for best; 'admitted' then lets the Royal Academician in near the start.
explanation.definitionFit: John Everett Millais was a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood of Victorian painters.

clue.text: Some criticise song or performance that's raised expectations

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, backwards
some means a part of, so the letters are a run within the words

explanation.surface: Some criticise a song or performance that was hyped.
explanation.walkthrough: SESONGORP is in the words; 'raised' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Prognoses are forecasts of how things will turn out, plural predictions.

clue.text: Draw attention to European, one having high standards?

parts.note: to flag something is to point it out
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A European draws attention to someone with high standards.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun: the standards are flags flown high.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole carries a standard, a flag, high up, so it literally has high standards.

clue.text: Boy that is tucking into sweets, they're often found near schools

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the boy and the abbreviation go inside the sweets

parts.note: lollipops are sweets on sticks
a lad is a boy
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A boy tucking into sweets near the school gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but it means going inside. In Britain lollipop ladies are school crossing patrols holding round signs on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: British crossing patrol staff carrying a round stop sign help children over roads outside schools.

clue.text: Syrup large American wears in court? On the contrary

indicators.note: wears means has on, so one piece covers the other
on the contrary reverses who is wearing whom, so the outer pair encloses the inner

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: A big American wearing syrup to court.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the large American would go inside; 'On the contrary' flips the container so they enclose the rest instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A linctus is a thick medicinal syrup taken for coughs.

clue.text: Rare items, old books vicar unwrapped

parts.note: ex means former, old
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer letters are taken off, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A vicar unwraps rare old books.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are unusual, foreign or rare objects collected as curiosities.

clue.text: Key cut

definitions.meaning: a key on a computer keyboard that erases
cut means remove or strike out text

explanation.definitionFit: Delete is a keyboard key, and to cut text is to remove or strike it out.

clue.text: Biscuit, e.g. turning rotten

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt or bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the abbreviation's letters E and G are used

explanation.surface: A biscuit, for example, starting to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning rotten' reads as going bad, but 'turning' is fodder and 'rotten' signals the anagram of EG and TURNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingernut is a hard round ginger-flavoured British biscuit.

clue.text: Deal with rant I dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry rant

explanation.surface: Dealing with a rant by dismissing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade with someone is to do business or deal with them.

clue.text: Pinched item of clothing

definitions.meaning: pinched is slang for took without permission, past tense
a scarf or wrap worn over the shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: Pinched is the past tense of steal; a stole is also a shoulder wrap or scarf.

clue.text: Bans maybe Cornish singer going round entertaining university

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the university letter goes inside
going round means turning back, so the region and singer are read backwards

parts.note: Cornwall is in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
an alto is a singer

explanation.surface: A singer from Cornwall touring and entertaining a university audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns SWALTO into OTLAWS; 'entertaining' puts U after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to prohibit it by law, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Very afraid oddly to stop one exposing greed

indicators.note: to stop means plugging a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the card word

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of afraid

explanation.surface: Someone very afraid of being exposed as greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of afraid; 'to stop' plugs those, after the V, into the card word.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a synonym of greed.

clue.text: Left off scratching head and relaxed

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so the first letter, the head, is removed

parts.note: left off means stopped, as in ceased

explanation.surface: Someone stops scratching their head and calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or made less tense, much as relaxed does.

clue.text: Point that's secured fair for football team

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so the point word holds the fair word inside it

parts.note: a stage is a point in a process
even means fair or equal

explanation.surface: A point is made that a fair result was secured for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevenage is a Hertfordshire town whose club plays in the English Football League.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage FC is an English professional football club, named after its town.
